name: Weight-Bearing Lunge (Knee-to-Wall)
instructions: Barefoot, second toe pointed at the wall. Lunge forward keeping the heel flat until the knee touches the wall. Slide the foot back until you find the maximum distance at which the knee still touches with the heel down. Measure big toe to wall, in cm.
target_description: Roughly 9-12cm is a common healthy range. Asymmetry beyond ~1.5cm vs. the other side is the meaningful signal.

name: Single-Leg Heel Raise Capacity
instructions: Standing on one leg, fingertips on a wall for balance only. Full-height heel raises at a metronome pace of one every two seconds. Count until you can no longer reach full height.
target_description: 25+ repetitions is the widely used normative threshold.

name: Single-Leg Balance, Eyes Closed
instructions: Shoes off, hands on hips, non-stance foot off the ground. Time until you touch down, hop, or your hands leave your hips.
target_description: 30s is a reasonable target for a trained adult under 40.

name: Y-Balance, Anterior Reach
instructions: Stand on one leg behind a line. Reach the other foot as far forward as possible, tap lightly, return without losing balance. Best of three, measured in cm.
target_description: Asymmetry beyond ~4cm in the anterior direction is an established injury-risk marker.

name: Side Hop Test (10 round trips)
instructions: Two lines 30cm apart. Hop laterally back and forth on one leg, 10 round trips, timed.

name: Single-Leg Hop for Distance
instructions: Hop as far as possible on one leg and stick the landing. Best of three.
target_description: Limb Symmetry Index of 90% or better (injured / uninjured x 100).

name: Thomas Test (Hip Extension)
instructions: Sit at the edge of a table or bed, pull one knee to your chest and roll back to lying. Let the other leg hang free. Note the angle of the hanging thigh relative to horizontal.
target_description: The hanging thigh should rest at or below horizontal. Above horizontal indicates a hip-flexor restriction that contributes to anterior pelvic tilt.

name: Standing Lateral Pelvic Tilt
instructions: Have someone photograph you from the side in a relaxed standing posture, or use a level app against your front and back pelvic landmarks (ASIS and PSIS), to estimate the forward tilt angle.
target_description: A neutral pelvis reads close to 0; several protocols cite roughly 7-15 degrees of anterior tilt as a common non-pathological range, so track your own trend rather than chasing a universal zero.

name: Anterior Core Endurance
instructions: Hold a modified curl-up or a front plank with a flat low back for as long as you can maintain the position without your low back arching.
target_description: No universal norm -- track your own trend.

name: Single-Leg Glute Bridge Hold
instructions: Bridge on one leg, hold at the top with hips level. Time until cramping or the pelvis drops.
target_description: 30s each side without cramping in the hamstring or dropping the pelvis.

name: Craniocervical Flexion Endurance Hold
instructions: Lying on your back, gently nod as if saying yes, creating a slight double chin without lifting the head. Hold as long as you can maintain good form without the neck's superficial muscles taking over.
target_description: No universal norm -- track your own trend; most untrained people fatigue well under 30s at first.

name: Forward-Head Wall/Occiput Gap
instructions: Stand with heels, hips, and shoulder blades against a wall. Without tipping your chin up, try to touch the back of your head to the wall. Measure the remaining gap in cm.
target_description: Smaller gap generally indicates more available upper-cervical range; track trend, not an absolute target.

name: Cervical Rotation Range of Motion
instructions: Seated, rotate your head fully to one side without moving your shoulders, noting how far your chin travels relative to your shoulder. Repeat to the other side.
target_description: Roughly 80 degrees each side is a commonly cited normal range.

name: Wall Slide / Overhead Reach
instructions: Back to a wall, heels a few inches out, low back flattened against the wall. Raise both arms overhead, trying to keep wrists, elbows, and low back in contact.
target_description: Arms reach overhead without the low back arching off the wall.

name: Apley Scratch
instructions: Reach one hand over the shoulder down the back, the other up the back from below. Measure the gap between fingertips.
target_description: Asymmetry greater than a few centimetres points to a rotational restriction on one side.

name: Supine External Rotation at 90
instructions: Lying down, shoulder abducted 90, elbow bent 90, rotate the forearm back toward the floor.

name: Sleeper Stretch Position (Internal Rotation)
instructions: Side-lying on the shoulder being tested, arm at 90, gently rotate the forearm toward the floor.
target_description: A deficit greater than ~20 compared with the other side is worth addressing.

name: Push-Up Plus / Scapular Control
instructions: In a push-up position, protract the shoulder blades at the top and retract at the bottom, slowly.
